topics.label: Introduction and lecture learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture series and sets out what students should learn from this lecture.

topics.label: Cellular changes, differentiation and tissue organisation in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish cancer as a disruption of normal cellular programmes whose development must be understood in the context of organised tissues.

topics.label: Distinguishing benign and malignant tumours through invasion and metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how tumour spread distinguishes malignancy from benign growth and demonstrate how that distinction is recognised clinically and histologically.

topics.label: Benign tumour progression and clinical significance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the possible course of benign tumours, showing that progression to invasive cancer is neither inevitable nor necessary for a tumour to cause serious harm.

topics.label: Tumour nomenclature
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how tumour names convey tissue of origin and malignant status, including exceptions to the naming conventions.

topics.label: How cancer causes illness and death
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how tumour growth disrupts normal bodily function and ultimately causes morbidity and mortality.

topics.label: Tumour incidence in humans and other animals
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics compare the occurrence of tumour types across populations and species.

topics.label: Clinical detection and cancer screening
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain why early cancer detection is difficult and assess how effectively screening can identify treatable disease at different anatomical sites.

topics.label: Lecture close and follow-up
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic closes the lecture by returning to the learning outcomes and directing students towards revision and upcoming practicals.
